items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Diabelli published an enormous amount of guitar music.

ctx.x: guitar virtuosi but virtuosi in general outside of that strict classical canon, they were not included. And the level of musicianship that — it is very tangible. That it wasn’t just that they were developing technique. Aguado, who is pretty much the father of modern classical guitar technique, he was kind of the pedagogue, really the principal pedagogue. Fernando Sor, for example, was a very accomplished composer. He was a songwriter, he wrote a vocal method, he wrote a guitar method. He played guitar with really…
method books, they published, they made their money, as much as they could, on publishing. Diabelli published an enormous amount of guitar music.
Well you were, before we turned the camera on, you were saying you perform tomorrow night, and then the “real” gigs start. And I wondered what that means.
